marvis.data.dataset.load_dataset(dataset_name, bypass_size_check=False, preserve_regression=False)[source]

Load a dataset from OpenML. Can load datasets by name or ID.

Parameters:

  • dataset_name (str) – Name or ID of the dataset to load. If using a name, it can be one of the predefined datasets (use list_available_datasets() to see options) or any other OpenML dataset name. If using an ID, it should be a string representation of the OpenML dataset ID (e.g., ‘1169’ for Airlines).

  • bypass_size_check (bool) – If True, bypasses the minimum 1000 samples requirement. Default is False.

  • preserve_regression (bool) – If True, preserves continuous targets for regression tasks instead of converting them to classification. Default is False.

Returns:

Features y: Labels categorical_indicator: Boolean list indicating categorical features attribute_names: List of feature names dataset_name: Full name of the dataset

Return type:

X

marvis.data.embeddings.get_tabpfn_embeddings(X_train, y_train, X_test, max_samples=3000, embedding_size=1000, cache_dir=None, dataset_name=None, force_recompute=False, task_type='classification', seed=42)[source]

Get TabPFN embeddings with improved class balance checking and caching.

Parameters:

  • X_train (ndarray) – Training features

  • y_train (ndarray) – Training labels

  • X_test (ndarray) – Test features

  • max_samples (int) – Maximum number of samples to use from training set

  • embedding_size (int) – Size of the output embeddings

  • cache_dir (str | None) – Directory to store cached embeddings. If None, caching is disabled.

  • dataset_name (str | None) – Optional name of the dataset for the cache filename

  • force_recompute (bool) – If True, ignore cache and recompute embeddings

  • task_type (str) – Type of task - “classification” or “regression”

  • seed (int) – Random seed for reproducible feature selection and sampling

Returns:

TabPFN embeddings for training set val_embeddings: Always None (validation embeddings no longer generated) test_embeddings: TabPFN embeddings for test set tabpfn: Fitted TabPFN model y_train_sample: Labels for the sampled training set

Return type:

train_embeddings

marvis.data.embeddings.get_embeddings_in_chunks(model, X, dataset_name='dataset', max_chunk_size=3000, embedding_method=None)[source]

Process embeddings for larger datasets in chunks to avoid memory issues.

This function is designed to process large datasets in manageable chunks, reducing memory usage and preventing out-of-memory errors. It’s particularly useful for validation and test sets that might be too large to process at once.

Parameters:

  • model (Any) – Fitted model with get_embeddings method or custom function

  • X (ndarray) – Feature matrix to get embeddings for

  • dataset_name (str) – Name of the dataset for logging (for informational purposes)

  • max_chunk_size (int) – Maximum number of samples to process in a single chunk

  • embedding_method (Callable[[Any, ndarray], ndarray] | None) – Optional custom function to get embeddings (default: model.get_embeddings) If provided, will be called as: embedding_method(model, X_chunk)

Returns:

Processed embeddings as a numpy array

Return type:

ndarray

Example

```python # Using default method (model.get_embeddings) test_embeddings = get_embeddings_in_chunks(tabpfn, X_test, “test”, max_chunk_size=2000)

# Using custom embedding function def custom_embedder(model, data):

return model.embed_data(data, special_flag=True)

test_embeddings = get_embeddings_in_chunks(model, X_test, “test”,

max_chunk_size=1500, embedding_method=custom_embedder)

```

  • random_state (int | None) – Random seed for reproducible sampling

Returns:

Array of shape [num_embeddings, embedding_dim] class_labels: Array of shape [num_embeddings] with corresponding labels

Return type:

embeddings

    Name of the DINOV2 model to load. Options: Standard models: - “dinov2_vits14”: ViT-Small with patch size 14 - “dinov2_vitb14”: ViT-Base with patch size 14 - “dinov2_vitl14”: ViT-Large with patch size 14 - “dinov2_vitg14”: ViT-Giant with patch size 14

    Linear classifier variants (with classification head): - “dinov2_vits14_lc”: ViT-Small with linear classifier - “dinov2_vitb14_lc”: ViT-Base with linear classifier - “dinov2_vitl14_lc”: ViT-Large with linear classifier - “dinov2_vitg14_lc”: ViT-Giant with linear classifier

create_visualization(train_embeddings, train_data, test_embeddings, test_data=None, highlight_test_idx=None, semantic_axes_labels=None, **kwargs)[source]

Create complete t-SNE visualization.

This single method replaces all 14 original functions: - create_tsne_visualization / create_tsne_3d_visualization - create_combined_tsne_plot / create_combined_tsne_3d_plot - create_tsne_plot_with_knn / create_tsne_3d_plot_with_knn - create_regression_tsne_visualization / create_regression_tsne_3d_visualization - create_combined_regression_tsne_plot / create_combined_regression_tsne_3d_plot - create_regression_tsne_plot_with_knn / create_regression_tsne_3d_plot_with_knn - And more…

Parameters:

  • train_embeddings (ndarray) – Training embeddings [n_train, embedding_dim]

  • train_data (ndarray) – Training labels (classification) or targets (regression) [n_train]

  • test_embeddings (ndarray) – Test embeddings [n_test, embedding_dim]

  • test_data (ndarray | None) – Test labels/targets [n_test] (optional)

  • highlight_test_idx (int | None) – Index of test point to highlight

  • semantic_axes_labels (Dict[str, str] | None) – Optional semantic axes labels

t-SNE coordinates for training data [n_train, 2 or 3] test_coords: t-SNE coordinates for test data [n_test, 2 or 3] fig: Matplotlib figure legend_text: Legend description metadata: Plot metadata dictionary

train_coords

Utilities

Utilities for loading and handling CSV datasets with precomputed embeddings.

marvis.data.csv_utils.is_csv_dataset(dataset_id)[source]

Determine if a dataset ID corresponds to a CSV dataset rather than an OpenML dataset.

Parameters:

dataset_id (str) – The dataset identifier

Returns:

True if this appears to be a CSV dataset, False if it’s likely an OpenML dataset

Return type:

bool

marvis.data.csv_utils.find_csv_file(dataset_id, search_dirs)[source]

Search for a CSV file in multiple directories. Uses robust resource manager search strategy with fallback to legacy method.

Parameters:

  • dataset_id (str) – The dataset identifier

  • search_dirs (List[str]) – List of directories to search in

Returns:

Path to the CSV file if found, None otherwise

Return type:

str | None

marvis.data.csv_utils.load_csv_dataset(file_path)[source]

Load a dataset from a CSV file. Handles both single CSV files with features+labels and separate X/y files.

Parameters:

file_path (str) – Path to the CSV file

Returns:

Features y: Labels categorical_indicator: Boolean list indicating categorical features attribute_names: List of feature names dataset_name: Name of the dataset (derived from file name)

Return type:

X

marvis.data.csv_utils.load_dataset_with_metadata(dataset_dir)[source]

Load dataset metadata from a directory containing precomputed embeddings.

Parameters:

dataset_dir (str) – Directory containing dataset files and metadata

Returns:

Dictionary containing dataset metadata including ID, name, is_csv flag, etc.

Return type:

Dict[str, Any]

marvis.data.csv_utils.find_csv_with_fallbacks(dataset_id, primary_dir=None, data_dir=None, embed_dir=None)[source]

Find a CSV file using multiple fallback directories. Uses the new resource manager for robust path resolution.

Parameters:

  • dataset_id (str) – The dataset identifier

  • primary_dir (str | None) – Primary directory to search (e.g., current embedding directory)

Path to the CSV file if found, None otherwise

str | None
